en: A Fragmentary Persian Scripture from Dunhuang, formerly housed in the Mogao Caves and now preserved in the National Library of China: *Yiji Congcan* (Collection of Lost and Fragmentary Texts), Volume Fifteen, Fragmentary Manuscript Scroll One.
The first half is already missing, while the second half remains intact; however, it lacks a concluding title. My friend Mr.

Li Zhenggang of Linchuan has verified that this text specifically elucidates the principles of manifest light and hidden darkness, corroborating them with the *Sanwei Mengdu* (The Three Powers of the Illumined Teaching).

Because there were points of agreement in its praises, it was subsequently established as a scripture of the Jingjiao (Nestorian) tradition. However, upon examination, the Great Ātman Māni bears considerable resemblance to the Jingjiao, making them difficult to distinguish; furthermore, both entered the Middle Kingdom from Persia. Therefore, for the time being, I have provisionally titled this "The Scripture of the Persian Religion," awaiting the verification of contemporary scholars of religion. Recorded by Luo Zhenyu of Shangyu on the third day of the third month in the third year of the Xuanchong era.
"□□□□ If one does not encounter the necessary conditions, there is no way to liberate oneself and seek understanding. □□□□□□ Regarding the nature of the physical body:
is it one, or is it two?"
All the noble ones appear in the world;
they employ skillful means to rescue and clarify the nature [of beings].
Having attained liberation from all suffering and ultimate peace and happiness,
he asked this question.
Bowing with reverence,
he withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time...
The enlightened messenger said to Āṭavaka,
"Excellent, excellent!
You act for the benefit of immeasurable sentient beings."
That you are able to inquire about such a profound and secret meaning—
you are now a great spiritual friend to all the blind and deluded beings of the world.
I shall analyze and explain it for you.
I shall cause your net of doubt to be severed forever without remainder. You should know this:
before this world was established...
The two luminous messengers— the pure wind and the virtuous mother—
enter the dark pit of the realm of ignorance;
they pull out the brave and robust one who is clad in the armor of great wisdom.
In the fifth watch, he clarifies his body,
exerts himself, and advances,
causing it to emerge from the five pits.
These five classes of māras adhere to the bodies of the five vidyās,
like flies stuck in honey or birds caught in birdlime.
Like a fish swallowing a hook;
for this reason, the pure wind acts as a clear messenger.
Through the union of the two powers of the five classes of māras and the five vidyā-bodies,
the world of ten directions and eight earths was formed; such is this world.
This is precisely the medical hall for clarifying the body,
yet it is also the prison for binding and restraining by the dark Māra;
therein lie that pure wind and the virtuous mother.
By means of skillful expedients, he established the ten directions.

Next, he placed the wheel of karma, the palaces of the sun and moon, as well as the eight lower stages, the three robes, the three wheels, and even the three calamities; the Iron Ring Mountains, the four enclosures, Mount Meru, the various minor mountains, the great oceans, and the rivers.
Having performed such acts as these,
he established the world and restrained the five classes of māras.
All were imprisoned by the thirteen great powers of light;
those thirteen types of great heroic powers—
the previously mentioned pure-intention winds and the five sons of illumination— bound them.
Furthermore, there are the *hulu-sed-zin*, *lou-yan-de*, as well as the *sulu-sha-luo-yi* and others.
These five bodies of knowledge (*pañcavidyāsthāna*) are like a prison.
The five classes of māras are like the five sons of the Purifying Wind (vāyu) among those imprisoned in hell;
they are like the jailers who oversee the prison.
To speak, listen, call, or respond—
just as when calling out at a watch-tower—
is the thirteenth *sūtra* on pārājika offenses.
Like a king adjudicating legal cases,
the Mara of Greed, having witnessed these events,
once again gave rise to evil schemes within his poisonous heart.
He immediately commanded Raurava and Karmāra to purify it with the winds of purity and the "Good Mothers" (Kulmātṛkā),
and therein to effect transformations and construct human bodies.
The prison confines the luminous nature and expands the great world;
such is the poisonous and evil physical body of greed and desire.

Although they are minute, each one emits the heavens and earth, the world-systems, the wheel of karma, the lunar mansions, the three calamities, the four surrounding mountains, the great oceans, rivers, the two lands of dry and wet, grasses and trees, birds and beasts, mountains and rivers, mounds and hills, spring, summer, autumn, and winter, years, months, seasons, and days, even down to all that is obstructed and unobstructed.
There is not a single dharma that does not resemble the world,
just as, for example, a goldsmith molds the form of a white elephant.
It was inscribed within the ring;
upon the body of that elephant, there was neither increase nor decrease,
even in the world of human beings.
It is likewise so.
That pure wind seizes the five classes of māras.
Regarding the thirteen kinds of luminous pure bodies,
they are imprisoned and bound,
not permitted to be free.
When Māra saw this,
he gave rise to a mind of greedy poison and bound his physical body with the five types of vidyā-mantras.
It constitutes a small world,
likewise imprisoned and tightly bound by the power of the thirteen forms of the darkness of ignorance.
He does not allow himself to be subject to it;
that Māra of Greed binds the city of bones with the breath of purity.
He establishes the signs of darkness and plants the trees of death;
furthermore, he binds the city of sinews with the wind of skillful means.
He establishes the dark mind and plants the tree of death; furthermore,
by the power of illumination, he restrains it within the city of the channels.
He establishes dark contemplation and plants the tree of death;
furthermore, he employs the water of wondrous skill to blockade the city of flesh.
He settled his mind in dark contemplation,
planted dead trees,
and further bound himself within a city of skin using the fire of subtle power.
They harbor dark intentions and plant the tree of death;
the demon of greed uses these five poisons as the seeds for that tree of death.
Planted within the five kinds of destructive ground,
it causes the luminous nature to be constantly deluded and confounded,
drawing forth that adventitious nature.
It transforms into poisonous fruit.
This tree of dark characteristics grows within the City of Bones;
its fruit is an enemy.
This tree of the dark mind grows in the city of sinews;
its fruit is anger.
As for the tree of dark thoughts,
it grows in the city of the channels; its fruit is lust.
As for that tree of dark thoughts,
it grows within the city of flesh;
its fruit is anger.
As for that tree of dark intention,
it grows in the city of Skin;
its fruit is delusion.
In this way, these five kinds— bones, sinews, veins, flesh,
and skin— form a prison that confines the five aggregates.
It is also like the five sciences that imprison all classes of māras;
furthermore, it subdues enmity and hatred, malice, lust, anger, as well as ignorance and the like.
He was appointed as a prison official.
Amidst the five valiant sons of the pure wind who had been released, he harbored greed and desire;
thus, like a shout, he spoke and listened, calling out and responding.
The fierce fires of gluttony and poison run rampant and unrestrained,
emitting *sūtra* and *pārājika* transgressions.
As for that body of the five aggregates,
having been subjected to such bitter and urgent confinement and bondage,
it has abandoned and forgotten its original mind.
Like one who is mad or intoxicated;
it is as if there were someone who,
with many venomous snakes...
They are woven into a cage with their heads all inside,
spewing venom in every direction.
Again, he took another person and hung him upside down inside;
at that time, the man was tormented by the poison.
Furthermore, being suspended upside down,
their minds and intentions are confused and disoriented,
leaving them no leisure for reflection.
Parents, relatives,
and former joys— these are now the nature of the five aggregates.
Within their physical bodies,
they are imprisoned and bound by Māra,
suffering day and night.
It is likewise so. Furthermore,
the pure winds fashion two luminous ships to ferry the virtuous sons across the ocean of birth and death.
Reaching the fundamental realm,
they cause the nature of luminosity to attain ultimate peace and bliss,
[overcoming] the enemy Māra and the Lord of Greed.
Having seen this, they gave rise to a mind of anger and resentment,
and immediately fashioned the forms of the two genders, male and female, and so forth.
By releasing the two great luminous vessels of the sun and moon,
they confound the nature of clarity and cause it to ascend onto the vessel of darkness.
They are cast into the hells and transmigrate through the five destinies,
undergoing all manner of suffering.
It is extremely difficult to liberate them.
However, if a wise messenger should appear in the world...
To transform sentient beings and cause them to be liberated from all sufferings,
one first begins with the gateway of the ear.
He brought down the sublime sound of the Dharma;
subsequently, he entered his former residence,
upholding a great divine mantra.
He restrains all venomous serpents and various malevolent beasts,
not allowing them to act with autonomy.
Furthermore, he carries the axe of wisdom to cut down the poisonous trees and remove their stumps and stumps.
Together with all other weeds and filth,
he caused everything to be purified and the palace to be magnificently adorned.
Having arranged the Dharma seat, he sat upon it like a king.
Having destroyed the enemy kingdom,
he himself adorned the palaces and halls within it.
He established a precious throne and impartially adjudicated all matters concerning good and evil among the people;
his benevolent brilliance served as an illuminating guide.
It is likewise so. Having entered the old city and defeated the enemies,
[he established his rule].
One should immediately distinguish between the two forces of light and darkness so that they do not become confused;
first, one must subdue resentment and hatred.
One restrains [the mind] within the city of the bones,
causing the pure breaths to all become free from bondage;
next, one subdues anger and resentment.
Restraining [the mind] within the fortress of the sinews,
one causes the pure and wondrous wind to attain liberation;
furthermore, one subdues lustful desire.
Constrain them within the city of the channels so that their power of clarity may immediately be freed from bondage;
furthermore, subdue the wrathful ones.
He forbids them within the city of flesh,
causing that wondrous water to immediately bring about liberation;
furthermore, he subdues ignorance.
He is confined within the city of the skin,
yet he causes both the wondrous fire and the two demons of greed and desire to attain liberation.
Restrained within the interim,
the fierce fires of the poison of hunger are unleashed to run wild.
It is just as a goldsmith who,
wishing to refine gold,
must first rely upon fire.
If fire is not obtained,
the refining will not be accomplished;
such is the function of the light of wisdom.
It is like a goldsmith;
when his crucible is refined,
it becomes as pure as gold.
That demon of hunger is itself a fierce fire that smelts and refines the five aggregates.
Causing them to be purified;
the Great Envoy of Beneficent Radiance,
within the virtuous body.
Employing the fire of hunger brings great benefit;
such is the power of the five sciences.
Abiding in the essence of harmony,
one relies on those virtuous persons to discern and distinguish between the two powers.
Let each distinguish for themselves that such a physical body is also called a "former person."
That is to say: bone, sinew, vein, flesh, and skin;
enmity, hatred, lust, anger, and delusion;
as well as greed and lewdness.
In this way, these thirteen together constitute a single body,
which corresponds to the realm of beginningless ignorance.
The second dark night consists of the poisonous and evil thoughts of the Māra of craving, which are of an unwholesome nature:
namely, delusion, lust, self-praise, inciting disorder in others, anger, impurity, destruction, dissipation, death, deception, and the dark signs of rebellion.
Such terrifying nights of ignorance and the twelve periods of darkness are precisely the original manifestations of the signs and omens of the various māras.
For this reason,
the Great Wisdom of Illuminating Clarity employs skillful means.
In this manner, the physical body is weighed and the luminous nature is rescued,
enabling one to attain liberation.
From one's own five limbs,
one emanates the five kinds of giving to nourish and benefit the luminous nature.
First, from the appearance of light (*ābhāsa*), compassion is emanated;
this is joined with the pure vital energy (*prāṇa*).
Next, from the luminous mind (*citta*), the fully endowed [deity] is emanated.
Empower it with the power of vidyā-mantras;
furthermore, through the contemplation of vidyā,
manifest patience and empower pure water.
Furthermore, from the luminous mind, wisdom is emanated;
it blesses the pure fire *hulu seduṃ lūvaḍe*,
and blesses wisdom within the treasury of speech.
Its elements are wind, fire, water, compassion, sincerity, faith, perfection, patience, wisdom, and the *hulu-sede-zhilou-lan-de* along with that illuminating insight.
Thus are the thirteen [signs],
which serve as the prophetic verification of the Honored One’s clarity,
like the world of Pure Radiance.
One who maintains the complete precepts is like the sun;
the second kind of person is like the sun.
This is precisely wisdom.
The twelve great kings are transformed through the illumination of wisdom.
Like the full moon,
he was endowed with the marks of prophecy.
As for the third day:
From this point on, these seven kinds of *mahallaka* (senior monks) fundamentally enter the bodies of pure masters and monks,
emerging from the locus of wisdom and clarity.
One receives the five kinds of offerings and,
throughout the twelve periods of the day,
completes the full day.
This was like the case of Sūrasa;
it was a sign of great power and a prophetic omen.
Thus it continued for three days and two nights.
Regarding their preceptors, teachers, and even practitioners,
they all possess the signs and proofs of the two realms;
at times, they are even those from former lives.
They engage in mutual combat with the newly awakened wise ones,
like the Mara of Greed at the outset,
intending to invade the realm of illumination.
Such was the prophetic sign;
from that old acquaintance,
he emerged from the midst of dark poison.
He emanates various māras,
who then engage in physical combat with the new person;
if the new person does not guard against the signs of their own past karma, [the māras will prevail].
Having forgotten the clear signs,
there will immediately be recorded omens;
such a person lacks compassion in their conduct.
When encountering matters, resentment arises;
this immediately defiles the luminous nature,
the essence of the pure aspect.
The nature of a guest dwelling there is likewise damaged; if it is to be protected,
[one must act accordingly].
Awakened by the signs of karmic retribution,
one should drive away enmity and hatred,
and instead practice compassion.
The nature and characteristics of clarity manifest,
returning once more to purity;
they are merely guests residing within the nature of the mind.
Freed from all perils and calamities,
they departed with joyful exultation,
having paid their respects and offered thanks.
At times, when a new practitioner forgets their mindfulness,
various māras manifest from within their obscured mind and immediately engage in battle with the new practitioner's mind.
That person possesses great signs of past karma,
yet they lack sincerity and faith in their conduct;
they give rise to anger at every encounter.
The nature of a temporary guest is immediately defiled;
such is the luminous nature of the mind's essence.
If you again bring it to mind and do not forget your original mind,
cause awareness to drive it away.
Anger and resentment were dispelled;
sincerity and faith remained as before;
and the nature of the resident guest was entrusted.
They are liberated from all sufferings and reach their fundamental realm.
At times, however, new practitioners may forget their mindfulness.
Thus, one is enveloped by ignorance;
from within the poison of dark thoughts,
various māras are manifested.
Together with that new person, they will contend in battle for the sake of the pure body of mindfulness;
there shall be a great sign of accomplishment regarding this person,
yet in their practice, they will lack full completion.
When the mind of desire is fervent,
the nature of the guest-like dweller will immediately be defiled.
If such a person maintains mindfulness and does not forget,
they will be well able to guard their perfected integrity.
He crushes all thoughts of desire so that they do not arise again,
dwelling as a guest within the nature of the mind.
They are liberated from all sufferings;
simultaneously purified,
they reach the fundamental realm.
At times, within that ignorance-thought,
various māras are conjured forth and engage in mutual combat with the thoughts of the new person.
If such a person should forget their original intention,
there will surely be a recorded sign or verification.
Such a person lacks patience in their conduct;
they give rise to anger at every encounter.
Thus, there are two natures: that of the guest and that of the host.
They are simultaneously defiled;
if such a person remembers it and does not forget, [the result follows].
Upon awakening, he resisted his adversary;
his anger subsided, yielding to the great power of patience.
One should further support and protect them;
as for those who dwell as guests,
their natures will joyfully attain liberation.
The fundamental nature is luminous and clear;
the essence of thought remains as it was.
At times, within the mind that is shrouded by ignorance, [it is thus].
He conjures forth various māras,
who then engage in battle with the mental substance of the new person;
if that person is [as described], [the māras cannot prevail].
Having forgotten their original intention,
there will surely be signs of karmic retribution;
such a person will be largely deluded in their conduct.
Both the nature of the guest and the nature of the host are defiled;
such is the case for this person.
Remember this so as not to forget it;
should ignorance arise,
you must immediately awaken to it yourself.
One will be able to swiftly subdue [the afflictions], exert diligent effort,
and achieve wisdom.
The nature of those who dwell as guests becomes pure for both, due to their wholesome karma.
The nature and substance of the mind are luminous and profoundly still, free from defilement.
These are the five kinds.
In that great battle between new and old men,
there was at one time a single engagement.
Consequently, the newcomer uses these five kinds of power to defend against enemies.
Like the great world, through the prophetic signs of the noble ones,
he manifests out of compassion.
He who upholds the world is like a messenger of light;
through his sincerity and faith, he resembles the Great Kings of the Ten Directions;
and being fully endowed with all virtues, he resembles a victorious messenger who subdues Māra.
Patience is likened to the messenger Earth Store (Kṣitigarbha),
and wisdom is likened to the messenger Radiant Light (Prabhāketu).
It is for this reason.
The sages of the past and those currently teaching have spoken thus:
for one who has left the household life,
it is not the physical body with its limitations that undergoes conflict.
This is indeed unimpeded.
The poisonous natures of all māras battle with one another.
Teachers such as these, whose precepts are thus pure,
are equal to the various noble ones. Why is this?
He subdues the hosts of Māra and adversaries because he is no different from the noble ones;
yet at times, his own troops and followers may suffer defeat.
The Dharma-characteristics of Wisdom-Ming were broad and expansive as he traveled;
reaching the five kinds of worlds and immeasurable lands of new beings,
he entered the City of Pure and Subtle Characteristics.
Within that jewel palace, he arranged a Dharma throne and sat upon it;
this extended even to the cities of his mental recollections, reflections, and thoughts.
It is likewise so;
each and every one enters universally.
If its illuminating wisdom roams through the city of marks, it is thus.
One should know that the True Dharma taught by this Master is entirely subtle and wondrous;
he delights in expounding the Great Illumination, the Three Perpetuals, and the Five Greats,
and is fully endowed with supernormal powers, transformations, and all auspicious marks.
Next, within the Dharma, he speaks exclusively of compassion;
or, his mind may roam through the city.
You should know that such a teacher possesses the power of eloquence, the light of the sun and moon, palaces, supernormal transformations, and is fully endowed with majestic authority.
Next, regarding the Dharma, he speaks exclusively of sincerity and faith.
Whether he dwells in the City of Recollection,
one should know that this teacher delights in expounding the great marks, is endowed with the *sūtra*, the *āpatti*, and supernormal transformations, and remains in silent composure.
Next, regarding the Dharma, he speaks exclusively of its perfection;
or he may travel through the City of Contemplation.
It should be known that this teacher delights in expounding the five sciences (*pañcavidyāsthāna*) and manifests supernatural powers (*abhijñā*).
Next, within the Dharma, he speaks exclusively of patience (*kṣānti*).
Whether he roams through the City of the Mind,
one should know that this teacher delights in explaining the past, future, and present, and possesses mastery over the supernatural transformations of appearing and disappearing at will.
Next, within the Dharma, he speaks exclusively of wisdom.
Therefore, when a wise person carefully observes this teacher,
they will know in which land the illumination of wisdom resides.
If there are those such as the pure Indradatta who thus uphold the unsurpassed True Dharma and do not fall back until the end of their lives.
After his life has ended,
that former friend and his army,
through the power of the darkness of ignorance, will fall into hell.
There will be no time of escape;
you must immediately lead your enlightened army and your pure retinue directly to the realm of light.
Ultimately fearless and constantly experiencing happiness.
As the *Ārya-cakrasamaya-sūtra* states:
If the body is endowed with wholesome dharmas such as *vidyā*, *na*,
and *ma*, then the Radiance Father-Son and the Pure Dharma-Wind will always dwell and abide within that body at all times.
That which is the "bright father" is the unsurpassed Bright Honored One of the realm of light;
that which is the "bright son" is the radiance of the sun and moon.
The wind of pure dharmas is precisely the illumination of wisdom.
As the *Ningwan jing* says:
If one is not endowed with the wholesome dharmas,
such as pure radiance and great power of wisdom,
they shall all be fully present within one's person.
This is the new person whose merit is fully perfected.
You all, listen attentively!
O Great Envoy Huiming!
He entered this world, a city of inverted views,
a winding village,
and a dilapidated old house.
Upon arriving at the palace of Māra, that Māra of Greed,
for the sake of its destruction and ruin, [acted].
They construct new, defiled cities;
due to their own ignorance,
they indulge unrestrainedly in the five desires.
At one time, a white dove— a sign of the wondrously pure wind, the son of a valiant Dharma-son and a great sage— entered this city.
Looking out in all four directions,
he saw nothing but smoke and mist.
Having gazed upon the countless villages with their winding enclosures and meandering paths.
Traveling by stages,
he arrived at the top of the city wall and looked straight down from afar.
He saw seven precious jewels;
each individual jewel was worth an immeasurable amount.
All were covered with various impurities that shrouded them from above.
At that time, the messenger Huiming—
First, take a plot of excellent land with rich and fertile soil,
and plant within it the unsurpassed seed of one's own radiance.
Furthermore, from his own body, he brought forth various forms and precious jewels for his own benefit and to generate great profit.
With various ornaments fully endowed, taking the internal nature as its supporting pillar, this true seed— the causal condition— produces from this pillar five layers of the dark pits of ignorance,
which are like a great boundary.
The winds of prior mental purity each have five sons,
which serve as supporting pillars for the bodies of the five vidyās.
Therein lies the field-tiller of skillful wisdom.
One levels and fills the rugged five stages of evil ignorance,
first clearing away the thorns and various poisonous weeds,
and burning them with fire.
Next, one should eradicate the five kinds of poisonous trees.
Once those five dark places have been completely leveled and destroyed, [the path is clear].
He immediately erected a hall and various palatial chambers for the new bridegroom.
Within that garden,
he planted all kinds of fragrant flowers and precious trees.
Thereafter, he first adorned his own palace, treasure seats, and tiered halls; next,
for the sake of the countless multitudes on his left and right,
he likewise constructed palaces for them.
By means of his wisdom and clarity,
and through his own majestic spiritual power,
he establishes these various kinds of accomplishments.
Furthermore, it overturns the dark realm of poisonous and evil craving,
causing its perversions to cease;
therein lies the fivefold pure essence of the luminous nature.
Gradually, they are able to be fully expressed.
As for those five constituents, they are:
appearance, mind, mindfulness, volition, and consciousness.
At that time, Huiming sent [messengers] to plant five kinds of supreme, radiant,
and renowned jewel-trees upon that pure ground of fivefold precious layers.
Furthermore, within the five kinds of radiant jewel terraces,
he lit five perpetually burning jewel lamps.
At that time, the messenger Huiming...
Having bestowed these five gifts,
one first dispels the dark signs of ignorance and cuts down the five kinds of poisonous, evil trees of death.
Its roots are enmity and aversion;
its trunk is stubbornness;
its branches are anger; and its leaves are resentment.
The fruit is divided;
the flavor is bland;
the color is loathsome.
Next, one must expel the darkened mind of ignorance and fell the tree of death;
the roots of that tree are, from this point on, devoid of faith.
Its stem is forgetfulness;
its branches are flattery and indolence;
its leaves are stubbornness and strength.
The fruit is affliction;
the flavor is craving;
the appearance is denial.
Next, one must expel the darkness of ignorance and deluded thoughts,
and cut down the tree of death;
the roots of that tree are none other than lustful desire.
The stem is indolence;
the branches are stubbornness;
the leaves are arrogance.
The fruit is derision;
the flavor is craving; the color is lustful desire—all impure karmas.
What was first becomes the lesson for what follows.
Next is the contemplation of pursuing darkness:
one cuts down the dead tree;
its roots, however, give rise to anger.
The stem is ignorance;
the branches are lack of faith;
the leaves are dullness and stupidity.
Fruit is contempt; flavor is arrogance;
color is disdain for others.
Next, regarding the intention to dispel darkness:
one must cut down the dead tree;
its roots are none other than ignorance.
The stem is indeterminate;
the branches are arrogant and dull-witted;
the leaves are preoccupied with their own reflections, deeming themselves peerless.
Fruits surpass all others;
ornaments and clothing are for adornment;
flavors are for enjoyment.
Adorning his body with necklaces, pearl rings, bracelets, and various other precious jewels is the nature of sensual craving;
partaking of food and drink of a hundred flavors is what nourishes the physical body.
Such a tree is called a "dead tree"; it is here,
in this dark cave of ignorance, that the Mara of Greed dwells.
Diligently cultivate and plant it;
at that time, O Hui-ming,
you shall employ the sharp and keen axe of wisdom.
Having completed the successive eradication, one plants the five kinds of unsurpassed, pure,
radiant jewel-trees within the fundamental ground-nature.
Upon those jewel trees, they irrigate with nectar-water,
producing fruits of immortals;
first, they plant the marks of the Buddha.
As for the characteristics of this tree:
its roots are compassion;
its trunk is happiness.
The branches are joy;
the leaves are the assembly of sheep;
the fruit is peace and security.
Taste is reverence and caution; form is firmness.
Next, plant the tree of the mind, which is a pure and wondrous jewel.
The roots of that tree are sincerity and faith;
the trunk is the manifestation of faith;
and the branches are fear and apprehension.
The leaves are vigilance;
the fruit is diligent study;
the flavor is recitation.
Form is peace and bliss.
Next, plant the tree of mindfulness;
its roots are already fully established.
The stem is good intention;
the branches are dignified deportment;
the leaves are truthfulness.
It adorns all practices;
its fruit is truthful speech,
free from false words.
Taste is said to be the pure, sublime Dharma;
form is the appearance that one delights in beholding.
Next, plant the tree of reflection.
Its roots are patience; its trunk is tranquility;
its branches are endurance.
The leaves are the precepts;
the fruit is the praise of the fast;
the flavor is diligent cultivation.
Form is diligence.
Next, one plants the tree of the mind; its roots are wisdom itself.
The stem represents the thorough understanding of the tenets of the two schools;
the branches represent the eloquence that elucidates the Dharma;
and the leaves represent skillful means and the knowledge of opportune timing.
He is able to subdue those of other schools and to establish the True Dharma;
as for his fruit, he is skillful in answering questions.
He speaks skillfully and spontaneously;
his eloquence is flavorful, employing apt analogies that cause others to attain clear understanding.
Its appearance is as soft as a lamb’s fleece;
what it displays delights the multitude. Such is this tree.
It was called the "Living Tree.
At that time, the messenger Huiming [presented] this sweet tree.
Upon that ground, he planted [seeds] within the subtle palaces and jeweled thrones of that new city, on all four sides,
and throughout the various gardens and groves— the natural state of the five stages.
Among these, the sovereign is compassion;
